highlights.description: `petstore-server` serves every operation of the Petstore OpenAPI definition from memory, so there is a real Swagger Petstore to call
The server can be an AAuth resource (`--auth aauth`): each operation requires the access its `x-aauth` annotation names, from the agent's identity to the person's approval of a scope
The OpenAPI definition is embedded in package `petstore`, with an `x-aauth` annotation on every operation
A static container image runs the server, with a built-in health check
The MySQL tools read their databases from a JSON file named by `PETSTORE_DATASOURCES` instead of an untracked source file, so a clean clone builds

added.description: Declare each operation's AAuth access level in the spec with an `x-aauth` annotation
Embed the OpenAPI definition in package `petstore`
In-memory store, seeded with six pets, and handlers for every operation
Route every operation from the spec; with AAuth enabled, guard each one with aauth-go's `ResourceGuard`
`petstore-server` command with `--listen`, `--auth`, `--url`, `--trust` and `--ca-file`; serves the spec at `/openapi.yaml` and `/openapi.json`
`petstore-server health` subcommand for container health checks
`petstore-server` container image on a static, non-root base
`create_pets` reports the host, server version and row count before it inserts
Postman smoke collection, mock server and agent skills
Data sources for the MySQL tools and the pet benchmark, read from the JSON file `PETSTORE_DATASOURCES` names, with an example file
`BenchmarkPet` runs against a configured data source and is skipped without one

changed.description: The MySQL tools take their databases from `cmd.LoadDataSourceSet()`, which replaces `GetDataSourceSet()` and returns an error; the file must not be readable by other users
The data sources file is opened once, inside its directory, and its mode is checked on the open file, so it cannot change between the check and the read
The Java example connects to MySQL 5.7 over TLS 1.2
The module builds against the published releases of aauth-go v0.3.0 and mogo v0.75.0

fixed.description: Handle the error from printing JSON in the MySQL tools
Clean clones build: the tools no longer depend on a file that was not in the repository

security.description: `create_tables` no longer prints the database password
Database hostnames and credentials come from a private file outside the repository, never from source
The upload handler's multipart parse is bounded by `http.MaxBytesReader`; the lint suppression says so

tests.description: Cover the spec, every operation and per-person orders
Run the Petstore behind the aauth-go sandbox as an enrolled agent, end to end
Cover loading data sources, including a file other users can read

documentation.description: Plan the Petstore server with optional AAuth
Describe running `petstore-server`, plain and as an AAuth resource
MkDocs site with a guide to testing AAuth interop
Describe the MySQL tools and the data sources file
Guides for running the server and the MySQL tools; interop guide uses the Compose profile for the Petstore
Release notes for v0.1.0 and v0.2.0

dependencies.description: Update dependencies; require aauth-go v0.3.0 and mogo v0.75.0

highlights.description: The Petstore `pet` table for MySQL, as SQL and as a Go function that creates it
`create_tables` and `create_pets` commands that create the table and measure inserts

added.description: `create_tables` command that creates the `pet` table in a named MySQL database
`create_pets` command that inserts pets and reports how long they took
JBang Java example that inserts pets over JDBC

changed.description: Convert tabs and update indentation in the Java example
